title: Stack
description: Describes the runtime-observable stack of a single project: languages, components (libraries/frameworks the project actually uses), and the canonical shapes of stdout lines those components emit. Produced by /detect-sensors as LLM-derived judgment from the project's manifests and initialization code; persisted at <project>/.harness/stack.json. Sensors authored against this project — particularly those with output: stream — derive execution.output_parsing.patterns[] from log_shapes[] rather than guessing. References: Boeckeler, 'Harness Engineering' (martinfowler.com); Lopopolo, 'Harness engineering: leveraging Codex…' (openai.com, 2026-02-11).

Role.description: Functional role this component plays. logger and log-encoder are split because the same logger (e.g. Zap) with different encoders (JSON vs console) produces different stdout shapes; the encoder is what determines the structured fields of the emitted lines.

Format.description: Wire format of stdout lines of this shape. json = single-line JSON object per line; logfmt = key=value k=v pairs per line; plain = unstructured human text; stack-trace = multi-line panic/exception trace (one Signal per trace, not per line); combined-log-format = Apache/Nginx-style positional access log.

FieldMeaning.description: Semantic role of the field, decoupled from its literal key. The same meaning may be expressed as 'level', 'severity', or 'lvl' across libraries — meaning=severity collapses them. Use 'other' as the escape hatch for project-specific fields that don't fit the canonical set.

Evidence.description: Pointer back into the project source justifying a component or shape detection. Mirrors the shape of Signal.evidence so audit tooling can treat them uniformly.

file.description: Path relative to the project root.

rationale.description: One sentence on what this evidence proves.

key.description: Literal field key in the log line, e.g. 'level', 'severity', 'ts', 'request_id', 'dd.trace_id'. The literal key is what regex patterns search for; meaning is the semantic label.

example_values.description: Sample values observed or known to be emitted (e.g. ['DEBUG','INFO','WARN','ERROR'] for severity, ['/v1/charges'] for path). Optional but strongly recommended — these are the oracle values the regexes derived from this shape are expected to match, and seed test cases for those patterns. NOTE: 'calibration' is reserved in this codebase for the inferential-sensor sense (cost.tokens, confidence_threshold) — do not conflate.

name.description: Library import path or canonical name. Examples: 'go.uber.org/zap', 'pino', 'logback-classic', 'github.com/go-chi/chi/middleware', '@nestjs/common.Logger'.

version.description: SemVer when extractable from the manifest; free-form when the manifest doesn't pin (e.g. transitive dep, range).

config_summary.description: One paragraph describing how this component is configured in the project, in enough detail that the LogShape it produces is unambiguous. Example: 'zap.NewProductionConfig() with EncoderConfig.LevelKey overridden to severity and TimeKey to ts_ms; sampling disabled.'

evidence.description: Where in the source this component is initialized or configured. Multiple entries are fine when configuration is spread across files.

id.description: Kebab-case slug unique within the stack. Examples: 'zap-prod-json', 'chi-access-log', 'panic-stack-trace', 'pino-default'.

produced_by.description: Names of Components (matching components[].name verbatim) that emit this shape. Multiple entries when the shape is a composition (e.g. middleware framing + structured logger payload).

fields.description: Structured fields present in this shape. REQUIRED in practice when format=json or format=logfmt — without it no regex can be derived; omitted for format=plain (no keys), format=stack-trace (positional), and format=combined-log-format (positional with implicit semantics).

severity_values.description: When any fields[].meaning='severity', the literal values the project's severity field actually emits. Examples: Zap default => ['DEBUG','INFO','WARN','ERROR','DPANIC','PANIC','FATAL']; Pino numeric => ['10','20','30','40','50','60']. Consumers use this to map verdict ranges (e.g. ERROR/FATAL → fail, WARN → warn).

sample.description: One real example line of this shape, exactly as it would appear on stdout. Used as a golden reference: regex patterns drafted for this shape MUST match the sample. For format=stack-trace, may contain embedded newlines.

version.description: SemVer of this stack snapshot. Bump on contract changes (components added/removed, log_shapes restructured, severity_values changed).

detected_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when this stack was last generated.

detected_by.description: Identifier of the producer. For LLM-derived stacks, the model id (e.g. 'anthropic/claude-opus-4-7'). For hand-written stacks, 'manual'.

version.description: Version reported by the project's manifest (e.g. go.mod's 'go 1.25', package.json engines.node, pyproject's requires-python).

purpose.description: One-sentence declarative description of what the application does in the world.

archetypes.description: Closed-enum archetype labels. Multiple values valid for hybrid apps.

journeys.description: Aggregation layer that UseCases reference via journey_id.
